def-randomized-complete-block-design:
## Definition

Fix integers $t\ge2$ and $b\ge1$. There are $b$ blocks, each containing the
same $t$ fixed experimental units, indexed within block $j$ by
$i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}$. The $t$ treatments form a fixed set $\mathcal T$ with
$|\mathcal T|=t$. A **complete block** is a block in which each treatment is
assigned to exactly one unit. The blocks and their units are fixed before
randomization.

Let $S_t$ be the set of permutations from the unit labels to $\mathcal T$.
The **randomized complete-block design (RCBD)** uses assignment space
$\mathcal Z=(S_t)^b$ and the uniform probability law on this finite nonempty
set. Thus each $z=(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_b)$ has probability $(t!)^{-b}$; the
within-block treatment permutations are independent and individually uniform.
This is a finite randomized-treatment assignment model
([[def-finite-randomized-treatment-assignment-model]]) whose units are the
$tb$ cells and whose assignment is the only randomness supplied by the
design. The design specifies no response model, Gaussian errors, additivity,
or absence of interference. A pair is the special case $t=2,b=1$.
lem-rcbd-nested-contrast-model-and-proje:
## Statement

Let $t,b\ge2$, $1\le q\le t-1$, and let $C\in\mathbb R^{q\times t}$ have
rank $q$ and satisfy $C\mathbf 1_t=0$. Give $V=\mathbb R^{t\times b}$ the
Frobenius inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{i,j}u_{ij}v_{ij}$. Write
$\operatorname{row}(C)=\operatorname{im}(C^T)$ for the span of the rows of $C$,
and define the full additive mean space
$$W_U=\{(\mu+\tau_i+\beta_j)_{ij}:\mu\in\mathbb R,\ \sum_i\tau_i=0,\ \sum_j\beta_j=0\}$$
and the reduced space $W_R(C)$ by the same formula with the extra restriction
$C\tau=0$. For an array $y$, write
$\bar y_{i\cdot}=b^{-1}\sum_jy_{ij}$,
$\bar y_{\cdot j}=t^{-1}\sum_iy_{ij}$, and
$\bar y_{\cdot\cdot}=(tb)^{-1}\sum_{i,j}y_{ij}$. Let
$RSS_U=\|y-P_{W_U}y\|^2$ and $RSS_R=\|y-P_{W_R(C)}y\|^2$, where $P_W$ is
the orthogonal projection onto $W$ ([[def-orthogonal-projection]]). Then
$$\dim W_U=t+b-1,\qquad \dim W_R(C)=t+b-1-q,$$
$$W_U^\perp=E:=\{r\in\mathbb R^{t\times b}:\sum_jr_{ij}=0\text{ for every }i,\ \sum_ir_{ij}=0\text{ for every }j\},\qquad \dim E=(t-1)(b-1),$$
$$RSS_U=\sum_{i,j}(y_{ij}-\bar y_{i\cdot}-\bar y_{\cdot j}+\bar y_{\cdot\cdot})^2,$$
and
$$RSS_R-RSS_U=b(C\bar y)^T(CC^T)^{-1}(C\bar y),$$
where $\bar y=(\bar y_{1\cdot},\ldots,\bar y_{t\cdot})^T$.
def-randomized-latin-square-design:
## Definition

Fix $t\ge1$ and put $R_t=\{0,1,\ldots,t-1\}$, with addition interpreted
modulo $t$. A **Latin-square allocation of order $t$** is a function
$L:R_t\times R_t\to R_t$ such that for
each fixed row the map from columns to treatments is a bijection, and for
each fixed column the map from rows to treatments is a bijection. Thus each
treatment occurs exactly once in every row and every column. Let
$\mathcal L_t$ be the finite set of these allocations and assign the uniform
law on $\mathcal L_t$. This law is well-defined: $L_0(r,c)=r+c\pmod t$ is a
Latin square, since adding a fixed residue modulo $t$ permutes the residues; hence
$\mathcal L_t$ is nonempty. This specifies one exact
restricted randomization law. It randomizes over treatment-by-row-by-column
assignments and is distinct from the product of independent within-block
permutations in an RCBD ([[def-randomized-complete-block-design]]).
thm-paired-randomization-contrast-moment:
## Statement

Consider one pair in the $t=2,b=1$ RCBD, with the two treatments labelled
$0$ and $1$. Let $Y_\ell(z)\in\mathbb R$ be unit $\ell$'s fixed potential
outcome under its own treatment $z\in\{0,1\}$, and assume no interference:
the outcome depends on the pair assignment only through that unit's own
treatment. Define $\delta_\ell=Y_\ell(1)-Y_\ell(0)$,
$\tau=(\delta_1+\delta_2)/2$, and the two possible observed contrasts
$$D_1=Y_1(1)-Y_2(0),\qquad D_2=Y_2(1)-Y_1(0).$$
If exactly one unit is assigned treatment $1$ uniformly at random, the
observed treated-minus-control contrast $D$ obeys
$$\mathbb E_d[D]=\tau,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_d(D)=\frac{(D_1-D_2)^2}{4}=\frac{\bigl((\delta_1-\delta_2)+2(Y_1(0)-Y_2(0))\bigr)^2}{4}.$$
Here $\mathbb E_d$ and $\operatorname{Var}_d$ average over treatment
assignment only, holding all potential outcomes fixed. The variance depends
on baseline outcomes as well as effect heterogeneity.
lem-randomly-selected-unit-effect-moment:
## Statement

In the two-unit, two-treatment paired randomization, let
$\delta_\ell=Y_\ell(1)-Y_\ell(0)$ and
$\tau=(\delta_1+\delta_2)/2$. Define $S$ to be the fixed treatment effect
$\delta_\ell$ of whichever unit $\ell$ is assigned treatment $1$. Then
$$\mathbb E_d[S]=\tau,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_d(S)=\frac{(\delta_1-\delta_2)^2}{4}.$$
The random variable $S$ uses both potential outcomes of the selected unit;
it is not the observed treated-minus-control contrast and is not a statistic
of the observed outcomes.
prop-rcbd-treatment-block-interaction-co:
## Statement

Let $t,b\ge2$ and observe one real response $Y_{ij}$ for each treatment $i$
and block $j$. In the additive mean model, the residual subspace consists of
the double-centered arrays
$$E=\{\gamma\in\mathbb R^{t\times b}:\sum_j\gamma_{ij}=0\ \text{for every }i,\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij}=0\ \text{for every }j\},$$
which has dimension $(t-1)(b-1)$ ([[lem-rcbd-nested-contrast-model-and-projection]]).
If a treatment-by-block interaction $\gamma\in E$ is included in the mean,
then the additive-fit residual is $\gamma+P_E\epsilon$, where $P_E\epsilon$
is the projection of the cell error onto $E$. For every $h\in E$ this same
residual equals $(\gamma+h)+(P_E\epsilon-h)$. Hence one observation per cell
does not separately decompose the realized residual into unrestricted
interaction and projected error, and fitting the unrestricted interaction
leaves zero pure-error residual degrees of freedom. This is an algebraic
design limitation; it does not assert nonidentifiability under every
additional stochastic model.
thm-rcbd-treatment-contrast-f-law:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $t,b\ge2$ and fix the RCBD cell layout. Let
$$Y_{ij}=\mu+\tau_i+\beta_j+\epsilon_{ij},\qquad \sum_i\tau_i=0,\quad \sum_j\beta_j=0,$$
where, conditional on the realized assignment, the errors are independent
$N(0,\sigma^2)$ variables with $\sigma^2>0$. The assignment law alone does
not imply these Gaussian, independence, equal-variance, or additivity
assumptions. Let $C\in\mathbb R^{q\times t}$ have rank $q$,
$1\le q\le t-1$, and $C\mathbf1_t=0$. Define $W_U,W_R(C)$ and their
residual sums of squares as in
[[lem-rcbd-nested-contrast-model-and-projection]], and put
$\nu=(t-1)(b-1)>0$. For the null $C\tau=0$, the statistic
$$\widetilde F_C(Y)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{b(C\bar Y)^T(CC^T)^{-1}(C\bar Y)/q}{RSS_U/\nu},&RSS_U>0,\\0,&RSS_U=0,\end{cases}$$
where $\bar Y=(\bar Y_{1\cdot},\ldots,\bar Y_{t\cdot})^T$, has the central
Fisher law $F_{q,\nu}$ ([[def-student-t-and-f-laws]]). In particular, the
usual all-treatment-equal test has $q=t-1$. This is model-based exact
inference conditional on the design, not a consequence of assignment
randomization alone.

The data space is $\mathbb R^{tb}$ with its Borel sigma-algebra; the model
above is the fixed-design Gaussian experiment for the realized RCBD layout.
